# Summary

In this report, we analyzed data within residents and directors, and then compared the groups' (*i.e.* residents vs directors) to one another. 

We found significant differences primarily in how directors and residents perceive different aspects of technical preparedness after residency, which are outlined further in the cross-comparison results. Analysis within the residents found significance primarily in whether they felt prepared after residency for various techniques based on if they had a cleft center in their program.

Significance was determined by adjusting for multiple hypothesis testing via the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure to control false discovery rate (FDR) for each family of tests: within-residents and cross-comparing the groups.

# Methods

We first tested for associations between questions and differences in means across groups (residents vs directors) using t-tests (for continuous variables) and Fisher exact tests (for categorical variables) depending on the type of question analyzed. Every question that was measured on an ordinal scale was converted to a Likert scale, and t-tests were thus conducted for difference in means. 

We computed Cronbach’s $\alpha$ for preparedness-and-education-related questions featured in question 7 and 8 on the residents survey in order to gauge the internal consistency of subquestions. This was only done within residents.

When we found consistency within question categories, we conducted additional analysis to see if median composite scores differed by subgroups. We did this using the Kruskal-Wallis test, a nonparametric version of ANOVA.  

We additionally created a logistic regression model to predict whether residents desire to be involved in cleft care after residency based on their program, the presence of a cleft center, and an interaction between them. 

All results are reported with significance, and when applicable, confidence intervals and plots, within the respective sections of the analysis below.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  if (question1 %in% c("education_lip_closure", "education_palatal_closure",  "education_expansion"       ,"education_orthodontic"      ,"res_prep_craniofacial"  ,    "res_prep_collab" ,          
  "res_prep_dental",            "res_prep_behavioral")){
   kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.numeric(df$response1) ~ df$response2)  
   return(c("question1", "question2", round(kw_test$p.value, digits = 4),  "KW"))
  }
  
  comparison_res <- df %>%
    group_by(response1, response2) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response2) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
  #table_hours
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4),  "fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
  }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), "chisq"))
}
```

  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(question_dic_res))) {

  res_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = question_dic_res$question1s[i],
    question2 = question_dic_res$question2s[i],
    data = i_res_coalesced
  )
}

res_results <- res_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = question_dic_res$question1s, 
    Question2 = question_dic_res$question2s
  ) %>% 
  arrange(Adj_P)

```{r cross-validation, echo = FALSE}
cross_validation_analysis <- function(question1, question2, data){
   df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      question1 = .data[[question1]],
      question2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
   
   if (is.character(df$question1)){
     table_comparison <- table(df$question2, df$question1)
     fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
     return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), "fisher", NA, NA, NA))
   }
   else if (is.factor(df$question1) | is.numeric(df$question1)){
     df <- df %>%
    mutate(question1 = as.numeric(question1))
    t_test <- t.test(x = df$question1[df$question2 == "Director"], y = df$question1[df$question2 == "Resident"], alternative = "two.sided")
     
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(t_test$p.value, digits = 4), "t_test", round(t_test$estimate[1],1),round(t_test$estimate[2],1), paste0(round(t_test$conf.int,2), collapse = ",")))
   }
}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
res_dir_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Test = character(), 
  mean_dir = numeric(), 
  mean_res = numeric(), 
  CI_diff = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(ncol(i_common)-1)) {
  res_dir_results[i, ] <- cross_validation_analysis(
    question1 = colnames(i_common)[i],
    question2 = "role",
    data = i_common
  )
}

res_dir_results <- res_dir_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = colnames(i_common)[1:(ncol(i_common) -1)], 
    Question2 = "role"
  ) %>% arrange(Adj_P)

```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}
```

# Cronbach's Alpha for Residents Q7 and Q8

We tried to combine the subquestions of questions 7 and 8 to see if we could create a composite score for each question, and we used Cronbach's $\alpha$ to gauge if the subquestions were internally consistent enough to do so. Both $\alpha$ values were extremely high, almost to the point of redundancy between questions, meaning that a composite score can be created for each question. The correlations for each question's subquestion are reported below as well. For both questions, each subquestion had a correlation of at least 0.64, showing strong consistency between subquestions.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
Q7_cronbach <- i_res_coalesced %>% select(education_lip_closure, education_palatal_closure, education_expansion, education_orthodontic, have_cleft_center, res_treat_cleft, res_instructed_all_aspects)

Q7_cronbach <- Q7_cronbach %>% 
  mutate(education_lip_closure = as.numeric(education_lip_closure), 
         education_palatal_closure = as.numeric(education_palatal_closure), 
         education_expansion = as.numeric(education_expansion),
         education_orthodontic = as.numeric(education_orthodontic))

Q8_cronbach <- i_res_coalesced %>% select(res_prep_craniofacial, res_prep_collab, res_prep_dental, res_prep_behavioral, have_cleft_center, res_treat_cleft, res_instructed_all_aspects)

Q8_cronbach <- Q8_cronbach %>% 
  mutate(res_prep_craniofacial = as.numeric(res_prep_craniofacial), 
         res_prep_collab = as.numeric(res_prep_collab), 
         res_prep_dental = as.numeric(res_prep_dental),
         res_prep_behavioral = as.numeric(res_prep_behavioral))

df_cronbach <- data.frame(Groups = c("Q7", "Q8"), Alpha = c(
  as.numeric(psych::alpha(Q7_cronbach[,c("education_lip_closure", "education_palatal_closure", "education_expansion", "education_orthodontic")] %>% drop_na())$total[1]),

as.numeric(psych::alpha(Q8_cronbach[,c("res_prep_craniofacial", "res_prep_collab", "res_prep_dental", "res_prep_behavioral")] %>% drop_na())$total[1])))

df_cronbach
```

## Residents Results

We found significance between all subquestions of Q8 about being educated on various topics compared to whether a resident's program has a cleft center or not. For each question, the mean difference was negative (see Resident Q8 vs Q2 results --- no composite score), meaning the residents who had a cleft center in their program feel significantly more educated than those who don't.

## Cross-Comparison Results

When comparing directors and residents responses, the grouping variable was always role: whether they were a resident or director. For each question the surveys had in common, if it could be treated numerically we conducted a Kruskal-Wallis test, and if categorical, a Fisher's exact test. We found that there was a significant difference in how directors and residents felt prepared for all subquestions of Q8. We also found a significant difference in whether residents were instructed in all aspects of cleft reconstruction including appropriate timing. The means and confidence intervals are reported below in the table. For each of the significant questions, the directors perceived residents to be more prepared than the residents responded to have felt, which is why the confidence intervals are all positive.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
res_dir_results %>% select(Question1, Question2, Adj_P, Test, mean_dir, mean_res, CI_diff)
```

## Q2x11x12: Association with cleft center/desire to be involved in cleft care post-residency/type of institution

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(modelsummary)

cleft_program <- i_res_coalesced %>%
  filter(have_cleft_center != "Unsure") %>%
  mutate(cleft_response = as.factor(cleft_after_res), 
         program = as.factor(program_type), 
         cleft_center = as.factor(have_cleft_center)) %>%
  select(cleft_response, cleft_center, program) %>% 
  drop_na()

cleft_glm <- glm(cleft_response ~ cleft_center + program + cleft_center * program, family = "binomial", data = cleft_program)

cleft_no_interaction <- glm(cleft_response ~ cleft_center + program, family = "binomial", data = cleft_program)
```

For this analysis, we performed a logistic regression model to predict Yes/No in question 2 as a function of Q11 and Q12.  We see from this model summary in Table 1 (above) that we have one parameter that is significant (being at a hospital-based program).  This means that relative to the baseline, which is a Combination (University + Hospital), someone in a Hospital based program is much less likely to answer Yes to Question 2. The coefficient estimate for hospital-based programs is -1.591, which means that if a resident is in a hospital-based program, the odds of them wanting to continue into cleft care are 5.13 (95% CI: `r round(1/exp(confint(cleft_glm))[3,c(2,1)],2)`) times lower relative to the odds of a resident in a hybrid program.  (Note: Odds ratio is computed as follows: $e^{1.591} =  4.909$)

We then added an interaction term between having a cleft center and program to see if there was an additional factor driving the signifance, but when adding the term in, the model was no more significant than the model without the interaction term. None of the estimates of the parameters were significant either. Additionally, in the model with the interaction term, the estimate for Program (Hospital Based) became insignificant, despite being so in the previous model. The model summary is reported below.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
library(tinytable)
library(modelsummary)

modelsummary(models = list(cleft_no_interaction),
             stars = T,
             gof_omit = ".",
  shape = term ~ model + statistic,
  coef_map = c("(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
               "cleft_centerYes"  = "Cleft Center (Yes)" ,
            "programHospital-based" = "Program (Hospital Based)",
              "programUniversity" =  "Program (University)"
                 ), 
  title = "Logistic Regression Summary: Predicting Desired Involvement in Cleft Care"
             ) %>% style_tt(
    align = "c",
    fontsize = 0.9,
    bootstrap_class = "table caption-top"
  )

modelsummary(models = list(cleft_glm),
             stars = T,
             gof_omit = ".",
             shape = term ~ model + statistic,
             coef_map = c("(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
                          "cleft_centerYes"  = "Cleft Center (Yes)" ,
                          "programHospital-based" = "Program (Hospital Based)",
                          "programUniversity" =  "Program (University)",
                          "cleft_centerYes:programHospital-based" = "Cleft Center (Yes) & Program (Hospital Based)",
                          "cleft_centerYes:programUniversity" = "Cleft Center (Yes) & Program (University)"
             ), 
             title = "Predicting Desired Involvement in Cleft Care with Interaction Between Cleft Center and Program"
) %>% style_tt(
  align = "c",
  fontsize = 0.9,
  bootstrap_class = "table caption-top"
)

```
